guides.title: Conversation and chat

steps.title: Find history and the composer
steps.body: The history contains your conversation; the message field at the bottom prepares the next turn. Read the current chat name before making changes. Enter sends a message and Shift+Enter adds a line. Opening this overview sends nothing; keep any draft you are already composing.

steps.title: Locate the conversation tools
steps.body: Save, Load, Memory and Controls sit around the history. Controls can show tools hidden on compact layouts. This course continues into the Conversation and Chat walkthrough, where you can practice sending a message, reply playback, editing and saving. Exercises wait for Continue, and setup elsewhere remains optional.

guides.description: Learn the Conversation workspace, then practice sending, replaying, editing and saving a chat.
guides.before_you_start: Read the existing values first. This guide opens the owning page without applying settings, starting services or performing tests.
learning_outcomes: Find the history, composer and conversation controls
Practice a short chat using the existing Conversation and Chat walkthrough
Replay, edit and save a reply, with each exercise waiting for Continue

guides.title: Visual Reply Preview Overview

steps.title: Inspect an existing picture
steps.body: Visual Reply displays generated pictures and can load an existing file. Use Load Image only when you want to display a saved copy; loading does not request another generation. If there is no picture yet, the empty preview is expected. Image-provider configuration belongs to Runtime.

steps.title: Read the image toolbar
steps.body: Previous and Next browse available history. Tools reveals actions hidden by compact layouts; Float opens a separate display. Clear affects the display, while Delete Image and Delete All remove stored files after confirmation. Leave deletion unused during this introduction.

guides.description: Visual Reply displays generated pictures and can load an existing file. Use Load Image only when you want to display a saved copy; loading does not request another generation. If there is no picture yet, the empty preview is expected. Image-provider configuration belongs to Runtime.

guides.title: Avatar Preview Overview

steps.title: Understand the preview
steps.body: Avatar Preview displays output from the configured avatar backend. It does not select or initialize that backend. If there is no active avatar output, an empty display can be expected. Runtime Session → Avatar has separate setup guides for the provider and its assets.

steps.title: Keep display and configuration separate
steps.body: Floating or resizing the preview changes where you see output. It does not prepare an avatar pack or repair missing runtime files. When diagnosing missing animation, note the selected backend and its status before changing the display. This overview leaves your docking and provider settings alone.

guides.description: Avatar Preview displays output from the configured avatar backend. It does not select or initialize that backend. If there is no active avatar output, an empty display can be expected. Runtime Session → Avatar has separate setup guides for the provider and its assets.

guides.title: Addons Workspace Overview

steps.title: Use the addon navigator
steps.body: The rail lists available addon destinations alongside core tools such as Persona, Addon Manager and Tutorials. Selecting an icon opens its page. Right-clicking an icon offers that destination's tutorials, even when another addon is selected. Hidden icons can be restored through the existing Unhide action.

steps.title: Choose a page-level guide
steps.body: Larger addons have several sections; simple integrations may have one page. Use the visible Tutorial button for the current page, or right-click its section. Provider addons appear under their Runtime category. The complete Tutorials library also lists broader exercises as workflows.

guides.title: Addon Manager

steps.title: Read installation and load status
steps.body: Find an addon by name and compare its enabled setting with its current load status. Installed, enabled and loaded describe different states; enabling an addon may require a restart. Read any reported failure before retrying. Viewing this page does not enable an integration.

steps.title: Inspect before changing an addon
steps.body: Read the selected addon's description and available actions before enabling, disabling or importing it. Changes can affect the next startup and existing integrations. Service-only addons are explained here even when they have no separate settings page. Preserve the current state during a read-only tour.

guides.title: Speech Timing Settings

steps.title: Understand chunk sizes
steps.body: Speech Timing divides reply text into pieces for synthesis. Smaller chunks can begin sooner but add joins; larger chunks may be smoother but take longer to prepare. Inspect the normal and streaming settings separately. Timing adjustments cannot fix a missing TTS backend or an incorrect output device.

steps.title: Compare one value at a time
steps.body: Note the existing value before changing a chunk or buffering setting. A later reply using the same text and provider gives a useful comparison of first sound and pauses. Restore the previous value if it worsens. Saved timing profiles and the active runtime configuration are separate choices.

guides.description: Speech Timing divides reply text into pieces for synthesis. Smaller chunks can begin sooner but add joins; larger chunks may be smoother but take longer to prepare. guides.title: Performance Check

steps.title: Understand what Start check measures
steps.body: Read Reply samples and Generate automatic sample replies before Start check. Starting arms a real measurement; visiting this page does not. With automatic samples off, you supply the replies separately. The result describes the tested provider, voice, avatar and streaming combination on this computer.

steps.title: Review recommendations before applying
steps.body: Read the sample count, measured reasons and proposed tradeoffs. Earlier first sound, smoother speech and lower memory use can conflict. Apply latest recommendation changes the recommended settings together; Load profile is separate. Keep the current values recorded if you decide to apply anything.

guides.description: Read Reply samples and Generate automatic sample replies before Start check. Starting arms a real measurement; visiting this page does not. guides.title: Tutorial Library

steps.title: Find guidance for the current area
steps.body: Choose the Desktop audience for NC pages, then browse the navigation-based categories or search by name. An overview explains relationships; a section guide stays on one page. Workflows are labelled because they may visit several areas. Your first chat remains the starting exercise.

steps.title: Read prerequisites before starting
steps.body: A guide preview lists what it covers and what is needed. You can read unavailable-provider guidance without enabling it. During a scoped guide, leaving its page pauses it; Return to tutorial restores the same step and End tutorial closes it. Remote-app guides retain their separate reader.

guides.title: Persona Tab

steps.title: Describe the companion
steps.body: Describe the persona holds your own concise identity instructions. Apply description as system prompt uses that text directly. Refine is optional and proposes a draft; inspect it before applying. These actions change instructions, so keep your current persona description if you only want to learn the controls.

steps.title: Check the active instructions
steps.body: Read Active persona system prompt after any deliberate apply. Generated draft text and the active prompt are different states. Save a reusable Persona when you want to keep its identity for later selection. If the result differs from your description, inspect the active field before asking the model to correct itself.

guides.title: Voice Tab

steps.title: Inspect the voice reference
steps.body: Read the selected voice reference and its available preview. A stored reference file does not prove a speech backend can use it. Check which Persona is selected before assigning a reference. If there is no sample, retaining the inherited voice is a valid choice.

steps.title: Apply to the intended Persona
steps.body: Use the explicit voice-apply action only when you want to change this Persona's reference. Backend compatibility and loaded TTS still determine how a later reply sounds. Auditioning a sample and assigning it are separate actions; compare the selected profile afterward.

guides.description: Read the selected voice reference and its available preview. A stored reference file does not prove a speech backend can use it. Check which Persona is selected before assigning a reference. If there is no sample, retaining the inherited voice is a valid choice.

guides.title: MCP Tab

steps.title: Read this Persona's tool access
steps.body: The MCP page controls which available tools this Persona may use. Review selections and descriptions before granting anything. Persona selection and MCP Core permission are separate layers; a checked tool here does not make a stopped server available or approve every request.

steps.title: Check effective availability
steps.body: Compare the intended selections with the status shown here. If a tool is absent, its server or registry may be unavailable. Review MCP Core separately after finishing this guide. Opening the tutorial selects no tools and executes no commands.

guides.title: Overrides Tab

steps.title: Inspect override categories
steps.body: Overrides separates Visual avatar tags, TTS voice provider tags, Language model and Conversation memory. An inherited value follows the shared configuration; an override changes this Persona's choice. Read the effective setting and any validation message before editing.

steps.title: Resolve drafts deliberately
steps.body: Keep track of unsaved override edits before switching categories. Review validation, then use the page's save or discard action as appropriate. Overrides need compatible providers and assets. A saved override records intent; a later controlled reply is the behavior check.

guides.description: Overrides separates Visual avatar tags, TTS voice provider tags, Language model and Conversation memory. An inherited value follows the shared configuration; an override changes this Persona's choice. Read the effective setting and any validation message before editing.

guides.title: Visual Tab

steps.title: Separate identity text from reference images
steps.body: A stable visual identity prompt describes lasting traits. A neutral reference image supplies reusable visual evidence. Importing a reference and generating a portrait are different actions; generation needs a working image provider. Inspect the accepted reference before creating a full mood set.

steps.title: Choose how references are used
steps.body: Read the controls governing self-images and mood portraits. These affect how later requests use the saved identity. Review one accepted image before generating many variations. If a preview is missing, check the selected Persona and reference status rather than repeatedly generating.

guides.description: A stable visual identity prompt describes lasting traits. A neutral reference image supplies reusable visual evidence. guides.title: Replies Tab

steps.title: Choose generation behavior
steps.body: Visual Reply behavior determines when this Persona may request generated images. Generate when asked differs from broader automatic behavior. Read the current choice before editing. Provider configuration and the Persona's generation policy both need to allow the intended later request.

steps.title: Separate generation from display
steps.body: Automatically showing a completed image controls presentation after generation. It does not cause an image to be generated or configure a provider. Keep the two choices distinct when troubleshooting: no generated picture and a picture that did not open automatically are different outcomes.

guides.description: Visual Reply behavior determines when this Persona may request generated images. Generate when asked differs from broader automatic behavior. guides.title: Library Tab

steps.title: Distinguish saved prompts from Personas
steps.body: The prompt library stores reusable prompt material. Selecting a library entry for inspection is different from applying it to the active Persona. Read its name and contents before using an apply action, especially when an existing prompt is already working.

steps.title: Review before replacing instructions
steps.body: Check a draft or imported prompt for unwanted claims and behavior before applying it. Keep a reusable copy of instructions you want to retain. If the active prompt changes unexpectedly, compare the selected library entry with the active Persona rather than assuming the model changed the saved text.

steps.title: Inspect imported identity material
steps.body: Identity Relay keeps imported companion material separate from your active instructions. Read the available artifact or staged content before applying it. A file being present does not mean it has replaced your Persona. The dedicated NC Identity Relay guides explain export and import operations.

steps.title: Keep application deliberate
steps.body: Review what an apply operation would change and which Persona it affects. Retain the existing profile if you only want to inspect the import. If expected material is absent, check the selected artifact and its status; do not repeatedly import unrelated files.

guides.title: Advanced Tab

steps.title: Read advanced Persona options
steps.body: Advanced contains options beyond the basic identity, reference and reply-policy setup. Note the current value and its explanation before changing it. Keep a working Persona as your baseline; advanced settings should address a specific behavior you can describe.

steps.title: Keep changes attributable
steps.body: Change one relevant option rather than several categories at once. A later short reply can help compare behavior, while the active prompt and effective overrides identify what was configured. Restore the previous value if a comparison worsens. This page tour does not send that reply.

steps.title: Inspect the context settings
steps.body: Conversation settings affect how recent dialogue is supplied to the model. Read the context-related limits and explanations before changing them. A shorter context can reduce how much earlier conversation is available; it does not delete the saved conversation file.

steps.title: Separate behavior from history tools
steps.body: These settings shape future turns. Editing or loading a chat happens in Conversation, and stored older messages have their own Memory controls. Keep the existing limits for this tour; later comparisons should use the same saved conversation and provider.

steps.title: Inspect writing assistance
steps.body: Read the writing-related switches and prompt text on this page. They shape the writing assistance requested from NC rather than editing your saved messages automatically. Keep a copy of custom guidance before replacing it.

steps.title: Compare guidance with later output
steps.body: A setting or instruction is not proof of a particular writing result. After a deliberate change, a later short example using the same request is a useful comparison. If it becomes too restrictive or verbose, restore the earlier text before changing unrelated model settings.

guides.title: Chat Behavior Proactive Tab

steps.title: Read when proactive replies are allowed
steps.body: Inspect the enablement, timing and instruction controls for proactive behavior. These determine when NC may initiate a reply during eligible runtime activity. Read their explanations before enabling anything; a stopped or busy runtime may not produce a proactive turn.

steps.title: Keep the first adjustment small
steps.body: Note the existing values before changing an interval or rule. Shorter intervals can make an enabled feature more frequent; they do not fix an unavailable provider. Use the displayed status and a later controlled observation to distinguish scheduling from generation failures.

steps.title: Separate summary from older messages
steps.body: Conversation summary keeps compact notes; Older messages stores past turns for later lookup. Their use-in-replies controls are separate from maintaining the data. A named saved conversation is needed for the associated memory tools. An empty summary does not mean the chat file was lost.

steps.title: Read search readiness before repair
steps.body: Compare saved, indexed and waiting counts. Waiting for an incomplete batch is different from an indexing error. Use repair or rebuild actions only for an identified problem. Keyword search and optional meaning-based search have different setup; inspect the current route before changing a model.

steps.title: Check readability in the current page
steps.body: After a deliberate appearance change, compare text, focus outlines and selected controls on this page. Keep a theme that remains readable at your normal window size. A display preference does not require loading a model or restarting a conversation.

steps.title: Distinguish a source from its policy
steps.body: Screen, webcam, clipboard and other sources provide sensory context. Their setup differs from the shared awareness rules controlling background reviews and replies. A source being listed does not mean it is capturing or that background use is permitted.

steps.title: Find the relevant source guide
steps.body: Choose the source you need and use its Setup, Prompts or Advanced tutorial. Orb vision and Spotify awareness have dedicated hosted tabs here. Inspect which sources and shared permissions are enabled before changing them; this overview does not start capture or grant background use.

steps.title: Read the capture target and model route
steps.body: Setup describes what the Orb can see and how its vision requests are handled. Compare the selected window, region or screen with the target you intend. Read the provider and model availability before enabling an auxiliary model; a selected name alone is not a connection test.

steps.title: Check readiness without widening capture
steps.body: Use the displayed setup state to identify missing requirements. An unavailable window should be reselected deliberately rather than replaced with broader screen capture. Viewing this page does not register a watch or grant shared background permissions.

steps.title: Manage only the intended watch
steps.body: Remove a test watch through its own control when it is no longer wanted, then confirm its row disappears. Hiding the overlay is different from stopping a watch. A new watch request belongs to a separate explicit interaction; this guide does not submit one.

steps.title: Inspect the Orb's behavior guidance
steps.body: Read the personality and reaction rules used for visual awareness. They shape how the Orb responds to context, separately from its cosmetic motion settings. Keep the current prompt while checking what target and provider supply that context.

steps.title: Make a controlled rule change
steps.body: If you need a different response style, record the earlier guidance and edit one clear rule. Avoid conflicting instructions across several fields. A later observed reaction is the behavior test; merely saving a rule does not prove a watch matched it.

steps.title: Check wording against the task
steps.body: Keep instructions specific to what the source can show. If guidance names information outside the chosen window or region, correct the expectation rather than widening capture automatically. A later explicit request can test the wording; this guide sends none.

steps.title: Recognize map and capture limits
steps.body: Compare the mapped region with the selected capture scope and current windows. Changes on the desktop can invalidate earlier locations. Read the map's refresh and diagnostic controls before using them; this tutorial performs no clicks on mapped applications.

steps.title: Distinguish a proposed action from success
steps.body: A target description or guidance beam identifies an intended location. Successful execution also requires the existing confirmation and verification path. steps.title: Inspect response permissions
steps.body: Read which awareness responses are allowed before enabling them. Background awareness and permission to control music are different choices. Keep the existing settings while learning; a later matching track and response provide the actual behavior check.

steps.title: Compare events before tuning frequency
steps.body: A repeated or absent reaction may depend on whether a genuine track change was observed. Check the displayed track information first. A later controlled song change is the useful comparison; changing several awareness and playback permissions together obscures the cause.

steps.title: Read how source context is interpreted

steps.body: Source guidance interprets incoming context; response prompts shape the reply. If the wrong song is identified, inspect the source data before rewriting response style. Preserve the previous guidance when experimenting so the interpretation can be restored.
